title: An agent's readback reads as a reply the orchestrator still owes a judgment
foundBy: session agent, from a live dispatch viewer run against the task-tracker challenge campaign tt-live2b-challenge-2, and the ALERT loop-speed's watch wrote into its record
details:
The readback is the dispatch create sends every member, usually `d001`, and create judges each answer itself. After create, `observe` still reads an agent whose newest dispatch is its readback as `node-replied`, "reply present, not accepted". The orchestrator's `wait` reads it the same way and says "idle replied to d001: read it, then `accept idle`". The dispatch viewer says the opposite: it notes an acceptance of a readback as `accept-of-readback`, because the orchestrator owes it no acceptance.

In most campaigns the orchestrator's first real dispatch replaces the reading within minutes. Orchestrators that run `wait` first are told to accept readbacks, and they do. SAC-102's record quotes a modeller's lost `d001` acceptance. The task-tracker challenge campaigns pair the orchestrator with an `idle` seat that is never sent a job, so the reading never clears. The watch that loop-speed runs alerted on it after 10 minutes in both such campaigns, tt-live2b-challenge-1 and -2.

The same campaign shape shows a second false alarm. That orchestrator worked alone and never wrote a log entry, so `output/log.jsonl` was never created, and the dispatch viewer reports `log-missing` as severe for its archive. The viewer cannot tell a log nobody wrote from one that was lost.

Wanted: once every readback has passed, an agent's readback reads as accepted, on the host and in the orchestrator's own tools. Also wanted: create makes an empty log, so an absent log means a lost one.
